fields.title: HEART: How to Choose What to Track in a Product
fields.keyTakeaway: A metric without a goal and a signal is just a number. First, "what do we want," then "what behavioral change shows this," and only then "how do we measure it."
fields.checkQuestion: Why can DAU growth happen alongside a drop in product value?
fields.blocks/0/text: The key question of this node: **what is currently happening in the product?** Any product has dozens of numbers, and almost none of them mean anything on their own.
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer this question.** The team looks at what is easy to measure: visits, installs, DAU. These numbers grow from marketing and don't show that people have stopped finishing what they started.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Five categories; pick the ones relevant to your task, not all at once
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Happiness** — what people think: ratings, NPS, post-action feedback.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Engagement** — how deeply people use it: actions per session, flow depth.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Adoption** — how many completed the key action for the first time.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Retention** — how many return and after how long.
fields.blocks/2/items/4: **Task success** — whether people complete a specific task and how long it takes.
fields.blocks/3/subtitle: The mandatory part of HEART that gets dropped most often
fields.blocks/3/items/0: **Goal** — what we want to achieve, in words: "owner creates a weekly schedule quickly."
fields.blocks/3/items/1: **Signal** — what behavior shows this is happening: "schedule is saved without edits within an hour of starting."
fields.blocks/3/items/2: **Metric** — how we measure it: "share of weekly schedules saved in a single session."
fields.blocks/4/text:
Goal: employee understands shift swap status without asking the owner.
Signal: after a swap request, the employee does not open a chat with the owner within a day.
Metric: share of swaps with no follow-up message to the owner — currently 41%.

By itself, "41%" means nothing. Tied to a goal and signal, it becomes a statement you can disprove.
fields.blocks/5/text: HEART describes the user value of a single feature or product, not the business. It does not replace revenue, margin, or acquisition cost. And don't pick all five categories at once: a set of five metrics that no one tracks is worse than one metric reviewed every week.
